15	  source: cloudbeaver
16	quirks:
17	  - "⛔⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR, AND WHEN: THE FIRST VISITOR TO FINISH THE SETUP WIZARD, UNLESS YOU CLOSE IT AT DEPLOY TIME. THIS IS THE SHARPEST QUIRK IN THIS FILE AND IT IS SHARPER HERE THAN IN ANY OTHER ENTRY, BECAUSE CLOUDBEAVER IS A DATABASE CLIENT: WHOEVER OWNS IT OWNS THE SAVED CONNECTIONS AND THE CREDENTIALS INSIDE THEM. CBApplication.java:224 sets configurationMode when the server name is empty, and the shipped config template defines no server name, so a fresh instance boots straight into the wizard. Set ALL THREE of CB_SERVER_NAME, CB_ADMIN_NAME and CB_ADMIN_PASSWORD (CBConstants.java:70-72) and CBApplication.java:349-400 finishes the configuration itself, BEFORE runWebServer() is reached, so the window never opens on the public hostname. Miss ONE of the three and the code logs 'No auto configuration was found. Server must be configured manually' and waits for a stranger. Do not rely on ServerConfigurationTimeLimitFilter.java:35: it expires configuration mode after 60 MINUTES of uptime, which is a limit and not a lock, and an hour is an eternity on a public URL."
18	  - "⛔ THE ADMIN PASSWORD MUST SATISFY THE SHIPPED POLICY OR THE AUTO-CONFIGURATION WILL NOT GIVE YOU AN ACCOUNT. config/template/cloudbeaver-base.conf sets minLength 8, requireMixedCase true, minNumberCount 1 and minSymbolCount 0. So generate at least 16 characters of MIXED-CASE ALPHANUMERIC with at least one digit. Alphanumeric is both sufficient (no symbols are required) and safest, because the value travels through a compose .env file and a shell and there is then nothing to escape. Brute force protection is on by default at 10 failed logins then a 300 second block (same file), so do not test the login with deliberate wrong passwords in a loop."
19	  - "⛔ THE ENV VARS ARE INERT AFTER THE FIRST SUCCESSFUL CONFIGURATION. performAutoConfiguration is only called inside `if (configurationMode)` (CBApplication.java:306-309), and configurationMode is false once a server name has been written. So changing CB_ADMIN_PASSWORD on a later redeploy DOES NOTHING: the password is already in the internal database. Change it from the UI instead. The flip side matters more: keep all three variables set on EVERY redeploy, because if the workspace volume is ever lost the server goes back into configuration mode and, without them, reopens the wizard on a live public hostname."
20	  - "⛔⛔ TURN ANONYMOUS ACCESS OFF. IT DEFAULTS TO ON. config/template/cloudbeaver-base.conf sets app.anonymousAccessEnabled to TRUE, and config/core/initial-data.conf puts the anonymous visitor in the `user` team. Two defaults currently limit the damage (grantConnectionsAccessToAnonymousTeam is false and the `user` team ships with an EMPTY permission list), which means the blast radius is one UI toggle away rather than one exploit away: the moment an administrator shares a connection with the `user` team, every anonymous visitor gets query access to that database. Set CLOUDBEAVER_APP_ANONYMOUS_ACCESS_ENABLED=false in the compose and verify it afterwards on Query.serverConfig, which reports anonymousAccessEnabled as its own field."
21	  - "⛔⛔ THE WORKSPACE VOLUME IS THE WHOLE INSTANCE, AND THERE IS NO SECRET KEY TO SET INSTEAD. Unlike every other entry in this library, CloudBeaver has no encryption-key environment variable you must remember: what it has is one directory that holds everything. server.database.url defaults to jdbc:h2:${workspace}/.data/cb.h2v2.dat, the generated H2 password lands beside it in .database-credentials.dat (CBDatabase.java:89-90,200-215), and the runtime config that records the server name and therefore keeps you OUT of the setup wizard is written to the same .data directory (CBServerConfigurationController.java:600-620). Mount a NAMED docker volume on /opt/cloudbeaver/workspace. Lose it and you lose the admin account, every user and team, every saved connection AND the credentials saved inside them, and the instance reopens its setup wizard on the next boot."
22	  - "⛔ ONE THING THIS RECIPE DOES NOT DO, AND SAY SO TO THE USER: THE INTERNAL STORE IS NOT ON THE MANAGED DATABASE. The managed Postgres in this plan is the database CloudBeaver MANAGES, not the database CloudBeaver stores itself in. Moving the internal store is possible in the community edition (CLOUDBEAVER_DB_DRIVER, CLOUDBEAVER_DB_URL, CLOUDBEAVER_DB_USER, CLOUDBEAVER_DB_PASSWORD and CLOUDBEAVER_DB_SCHEMA are all runtime variables, the postgres driver is bundled, and the schema directory even carries a Postgres-specific migration), but redu's managed Postgres serves EXACTLY ONE database, so CloudBeaver's own tables would land alongside the user's data. This recipe has NOT tested that combination and does not recommend it. If you do try it, note CBDatabase.java:188-189 throws 'Password must be specified for non-embedded database', so at least it fails loudly."
23	  - "THE POSTGRES JDBC DRIVER IS ALREADY IN THE IMAGE, WHICH IS WHY THE PRIVATE NETWORK IS ENOUGH. server/bundles/io.cloudbeaver.resources.drivers.base/plugin.xml bundles postgresql:postgres-jdbc along with mysql8, mariadb, sqlserver, oracle, sqlite, db2, clickhouse, duckdb, firebird, trino, kyuubi and databend, so nothing is fetched from the internet when a connection is created. Point it at redu's managed database on its PRIVATE address. After the deploy, read PGHOST, PGPORT, PGDATABASE, PGUSER and PGPASSWORD off the deployment and give them to the user to enter in Administration then Connections. Do NOT put those values in the container's environment just to make typing easier unless the user asks: see the systemVariablesResolvingEnabled quirk."
24	  - "CLOUDBEAVER_SYSTEM_VARIABLES_RESOLVING_ENABLED IS A REAL TRADE, NOT A CONVENIENCE FLAG. It defaults to FALSE (config/template/cloudbeaver-base.conf) and turning it on lets connection settings resolve environment variables, so a connection host could literally be written as the name of an injected variable instead of a pasted value. The cost is that anyone who can edit a connection can then read your container's environment, which on a redu deploy includes the managed database password. Leave it false unless the user asks for it and understands that."
25	  - "NON-ADMINS CANNOT CREATE CONNECTIONS BY DEFAULT, AND THAT IS THE GOOD DEFAULT. app.supportsCustomConnections defaults to FALSE in the production template (it is TRUE only in the test config under server/test/), so ordinary users work with the connections an administrator has created and shared. Leave it false. Turning it on turns every account into an outbound TCP client from your VM into your own private network, which is an SSRF primitive with a nice UI."
26	  - "PORT 8978, AND THE CONTAINER STARTS AS ROOT ON PURPOSE. The Dockerfile exposes 8978 and the registry image config confirms ExposedPorts 8978/tcp with no USER set. deploy/scripts/launch-product.sh chowns the workspace to uid 8978 and then drops privileges with `su dbeaver`, which is why a freshly created volume does not need its ownership set up first. Publish 8978:8978 and pass port 8978 to deploy_compose. Health probe: GET /status, an unauthenticated servlet returning JSON with health, product.name and product.version (WebStatusServlet.java:35,44-47)."
27	  - "LEAVE CLOUDBEAVER_FORCE_HTTPS AT FALSE. It defaults to false (config/template/cloudbeaver-base.conf) and false is correct here: TLS terminates at redu's proxy and the container is spoken to over plain HTTP on the VM. The user's browser still gets HTTPS end to end from the proxy. Turning it on makes the app try to enforce a scheme it cannot see."
28	  - "⛔ PIN FROM THE REGISTRY, BECAUSE THERE IS NOWHERE ELSE TO LOOK. dbeaver/cloudbeaver has 149 tags on Docker Hub, while the GitHub repo publishes ZERO releases and has no git tag for the current version at all. So a habit of reading `releases/latest` returns nothing here, and reading the git tag list returns a version months behind. Use dbeaver/cloudbeaver:26.1.4 (published 2026-08-03, sha256:«REDACTED:longhex:0d118806»). `latest`, `26` and `26.1` currently resolve to that same digest; pin the exact version anyway. ⚠️ There is also an `ea` tag, which is early access and moves ahead of stable; never use it in a recipe."
29	  - "NO migrate_command NEEDED. CBDatabase creates and updates its own schema at boot (createSchemaIfNotExists then updateSchema, CBDatabase.java:220-230), currently at version 29. Nothing external runs migrations here."
30	  - "SIZING IS AN ESTIMATE AND UPSTREAM PUBLISHES NO NUMBER. Checked the Dockerfiles, run-cloudbeaver-server.sh and the whole deploy directory: there is no JAVA_OPTS default, no -Xmx and no sizing note anywhere. m1.medium (2 vCPU / 4 GB) is reasoning from 'an Eclipse/OSGi Java server on ubuntu:noble with a bundled Temurin 25 JDK, where the JVM takes a quarter of container memory as its default max heap', so 4 GB gives it roughly 1 GB of heap and m1.small would give it 512 MB. m1.medium is also the trial ceiling, so there is no cheaper trial-eligible step up. Set JAVA_OPTS explicitly if you need to, and measure it on your run rather than repeating this paragraph."
31	  - "DISK: RESULT SETS AND EXPORTS LAND ON THE APP VM. resourceQuotas in the shipped template caps a SQL result set at 100000 rows and a running query count at 100, and the data-transfer plugin writes export files into the workspace before serving them. On m1.medium that is 40 GB of flavor disk shared with the workspace volume. Exporting a large table is therefore a disk event on the VM, not just a download. Growing it later is a volume resize, not a redeploy, so say it before sizing."
32	  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> generate CB_ADMIN_PASSWORD (16+ mixed-case alphanumeric with a digit) and pick CB_ADMIN_NAME and CB_SERVER_NAME -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.045/hr, roughly GBP 33 a month; fits the no-card free trial) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '3' (m1.medium), database:'managed', db_engine:'postgres', db_flavor_id:'2', port 8978. Pass db_flavor_id explicitly: omitting it defaults the database VM to the app flavor and doubles the bill. plan_deploy will want to upsize a compose stack to m1.large, which is right for things that BUILD from source and wrong here, since this image is pulled; passing flavor_id '3' holds m1.medium and keeps the deploy inside the trial."
33	  - "IF THE USER ALREADY HAS A DATABASE, SKIP THE MANAGED ONE AND SAY WHAT THAT SAVES. CloudBeaver does not need a database of its own for this recipe; the managed Postgres is there so there is something to manage. Deploying with database:'none' drops the quote from about GBP 33 a month to about GBP 20 and the app is identical. That is the user's call, so put it to them rather than deciding it. Whatever they connect to must be reachable from the app VM: redu's private network reaches a managed database directly, and anything outside needs a route the VM actually has."
34	  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built from source, and cloning is actively wrong here: upstream's build script starts by cloning two FURTHER repositories (dbeaver and dbeaver-common) and running a full maven build. Write the one-service docker-compose.yml locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo."
35	  - "LICENCE: Apache-2.0, verified by reading the file: 201 lines of the canonical Apache text, no Commons Clause, no addendum, and the two matches for 'addendum' and 'additional terms' are Apache's own sections 4 and 5. Self-hosting the community edition for yourself and your team is squarely inside it. Enterprise features and the DBeaver desktop product are separate offerings from DBeaver Corp and none of this changes that."
36	  - "DELETING IT LEAVES THE DATABASE BEHIND, ON PURPOSE. delete_deployment removes the app VM but keeps the managed Postgres, so the data you were managing survives, and that database keeps billing at GBP 0.0174/hr. ⚠️ The WORKSPACE VOLUME goes with the app VM, so the admin account, every saved connection and every saved credential are destroyed with it. That is usually what you want when tearing down a credential store, but say it plainly first. Use delete_database when the user really means all of it."

38	
39	# Self-host CloudBeaver on redu
40	
41	A full web SQL client on your own infrastructure: browse schemas, run queries, edit data and export
42	results from a browser, with a managed Postgres beside it on redu's private network and nothing in
43	the middle.
44	
45	## Read this before you deploy
46	
47	CloudBeaver is a **database client**, which makes it different from everything else in this
48	library. It exists to hold connection details, and usually the credentials that go with them, for
49	other systems. An unclaimed CloudBeaver on a public hostname is not an empty app waiting to be set
50	up: it is a credential store waiting to be taken.
51	
52	So the single most important thing in this recipe is that the **setup wizard is finished at deploy
53	time, before the port is listening**. CloudBeaver supports that natively, with three environment

146	#    error page fails every "did it NOT do X" check. A JVM this size takes a while, so be patient.

162	#    version and a name, nothing below means anything. Body on stdin, never in argv.
163	printf '%s' '{"query":"{serverConfig{name version configurationMode anonymousAccessEnabled supportsCustomConnections}}"}' > "$TMP/q"

167	  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: POST /api/ answered HTTP $code." >&2
168	  exit 2

172	  echo "  below out of a body this script could not identify." >&2
173	  exit 2
174	fi

176	# 3. THE ASSERTIONS. Each one requires the field to be PRESENT with the right value. A missing
177	#    field is inconclusive, never a pass, because a renamed field would otherwise read as success.
178	fail=0
179	if grep -q '"configurationMode":true' "$TMP/cfg"; then
180	  echo "FAIL: this server is STILL IN CONFIGURATION MODE. Anyone who loads the URL right now can" >&2
181	  echo "  set the administrator password and own every connection you add later." >&2
182	  echo "  Cause: CB_SERVER_NAME, CB_ADMIN_NAME and CB_ADMIN_PASSWORD must ALL three be set." >&2
183	  fail=1
184	elif ! grep -q '"configurationMode":false' "$TMP/cfg"; then
185	  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: no configurationMode field in the response. It moved; do not assume it is" >&2
186	  echo "  closed on the strength of an absent field." >&2
187	  exit 2
188	else
189	  echo "OK: configuration is finished, so the wizard cannot be used to claim this instance."
190	fi
191

193	  echo "FAIL: anonymous access is ENABLED. Set CLOUDBEAVER_APP_ANONYMOUS_ACCESS_ENABLED=false" >&2
194	  echo "  and redeploy before you add any connection to this instance." >&2
195	  fail=1
196	elif ! grep -q '"anonymousAccessEnabled":false' "$TMP/cfg"; then
197	  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: no anonymousAccessEnabled field in the response." >&2
198	  exit 2
199	else
200	  echo "OK: anonymous access is disabled."
201	fi
202	
203	if grep -q '"supportsCustomConnections":true' "$TMP/cfg"; then
204	  echo "NOTE: non-admin users can create their own connections. That is a deliberate setting;" >&2
205	  echo "  it also lets any account open TCP connections from this VM into your private network." >&2
206	fi

208	[ "$fail" -eq 0 ] || exit 1

210	echo "Last step, and HTTP cannot do it for you: sign in at https://$HOST with the admin account"
211	echo "you were given. A server can be out of configuration mode and still have credentials you"

A full web SQL client on your own infrastructure: browse schemas, run queries, edit data and export

CloudBeaver is a **database client**, which makes it different from everything else in this
library. It exists to hold connection details, and usually the credentials that go with them, for

- A named volume on `/opt/cloudbeaver/workspace`, which holds the admin account, every user and
  team, and every saved connection.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

#    assertion below is vacuous, because redu's proxy answers 502 while the container starts and an
#    error page fails every "did it NOT do X" check. A JVM this size takes a while, so be patient.
code=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/status" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/status")
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /status answered HTTP $code, not 200." >&2
  if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
    echo "  502 is redu's proxy while the container starts. Wait and re-run. This is NOT a pass." >&2
  fi
  exit 2
fi
if ! grep -q '"health"' "$TMP/status" || ! grep -q '"product.name"' "$TMP/status"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 200 from /status but the body is not CloudBeaver's status payload." >&2
  exit 2
fi
echo "OK: CloudBeaver is serving."

# 2. POSITIVE CONTROL. Ask its GraphQL API for the server config. If this does not come back with a
#    version and a name, nothing below means anything. Body on stdin, never in argv.
printf '%s' '{"query":"{serverConfig{name version configurationMode anonymousAccessEnabled supportsCustomConnections}}"}' > "$TMP/q"
code=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/cfg" -w '%{http_code}' -X POST \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @"$TMP/q" "https://$HOST/api/")
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: POST /api/ answered HTTP $code." >&2
  exit 2
fi
if ! grep -q '"version"' "$TMP/cfg" || ! grep -q '"name"' "$TMP/cfg"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /api/ returned 200 without a serverConfig payload. Do not read the flags" >&2
  echo "  below out of a body this script could not identify." >&2
  exit 2
fi

# 3. THE ASSERTIONS. Each one requires the field to be PRESENT with the right value. A missing
#    field is inconclusive, never a pass, because a renamed field would otherwise read as success.
fail=0
if grep -q '"configurationMode":true' "$TMP/cfg"; then
  echo "FAIL: this server is STILL IN CONFIGURATION MODE. Anyone who loads the URL right now can" >&2
  echo "  set the administrator password and own every connection you add later." >&2
  echo "  Cause: CB_SERVER_NAME, CB_ADMIN_NAME and CB_ADMIN_PASSWORD must ALL three be set." >&2
  fail=1
elif ! grep -q '"configurationMode":false' "$TMP/cfg"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: no configurationMode field in the response. It moved; do not assume it is" >&2
  echo "  closed on the strength of an absent field." >&2
  exit 2
else
  echo "OK: configuration is finished, so the wizard cannot be used to claim this instance."
fi

if grep -q '"anonymousAccessEnabled":true' "$TMP/cfg"; then
  echo "FAIL: anonymous access is ENABLED. Set CLOUDBEAVER_APP_ANONYMOUS_ACCESS_ENABLED=false" >&2
  echo "  and redeploy before you add any connection to this instance." >&2
  fail=1
elif ! grep -q '"anonymousAccessEnabled":false' "$TMP/cfg"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: no anonymousAccessEnabled field in the response." >&2
  exit 2
else
  echo "OK: anonymous access is disabled."
fi

if grep -q '"supportsCustomConnections":true' "$TMP/cfg"; then
  echo "NOTE: non-admin users can create their own connections. That is a deliberate setting;" >&2
  echo "  it also lets any account open TCP connections from this VM into your private network." >&2
fi

[ "$fail" -eq 0 ] || exit 1
echo
echo "Last step, and HTTP cannot do it for you: sign in at https://$HOST with the admin account"
echo "you were given. A server can be out of configuration mode and still have credentials you"
echo "do not hold, so the only proof the instance is YOURS is logging into it."

## What an anonymous request can reach

With this recipe's settings: `/status` (health, product name and version), the login page and the
static assets, and `Query.serverConfig`, which is what the login page reads to render itself.
Nothing else. No connection, no schema, no query.

With the **stock** settings, an anonymous visitor also gets a working session in the `user` team.
That team ships with an empty permission list and no connections are granted to it by default, so
there is nothing to see yet. "Yet" is the problem: sharing a connection with the default user team
is one click, and it silently turns that empty session into database access. Turning anonymous
access off at deploy time removes the whole question.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove this CloudBeaver is configured, owned by you, and not open to anonymous visitors.
#   ./verify-cloudbeaver.sh cloudbeaver-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
# Exit 0 = good, 1 = FAIL (fix it now), 2 = inconclusive (it may still be starting).
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-cloudbeaver.sh <host>}"
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# 1. GATE. /status is CloudBeaver's own unauthenticated status servlet. Without this gate every
#    assertion below is vacuous, because redu's proxy answers 502 while the container starts and an
#    error page fails every "did it NOT do X" check. A JVM this size takes a while, so be patient.
code=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/status" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/status")
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /status answered HTTP $code, not 200." >&2
  if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
    echo "  502 is redu's proxy while the container starts. Wait and re-run. This is NOT a pass." >&2
  fi
  exit 2
fi
if ! grep -q '"health"' "$TMP/status" || ! grep -q '"product.name"' "$TMP/status"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 200 from /status but the body is not CloudBeaver's status payload." >&2
  exit 2
fi
echo "OK: CloudBeaver is serving."

# 2. POSITIVE CONTROL. Ask its GraphQL API for the server config. If this does not come back with a
#    version and a name, nothing below means anything. Body on stdin, never in argv.
printf '%s' '{"query":"{serverConfig{name version configurationMode anonymousAccessEnabled supportsCustomConnections}}"}' > "$TMP/q"
code=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/cfg" -w '%{http_code}' -X POST \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @"$TMP/q" "https://$HOST/api/")
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: POST /api/ answered HTTP $code." >&2
  exit 2
fi
if ! grep -q '"version"' "$TMP/cfg" || ! grep -q '"name"' "$TMP/cfg"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /api/ returned 200 without a serverConfig payload. Do not read the flags" >&2
  echo "  below out of a body this script could not identify." >&2
  exit 2
fi

# 3. THE ASSERTIONS. Each one requires the field to be PRESENT with the right value. A missing
#    field is inconclusive, never a pass, because a renamed field would otherwise read as success.
fail=0
if grep -q '"configurationMode":true' "$TMP/cfg"; then
  echo "FAIL: this server is STILL IN CONFIGURATION MODE. Anyone who loads the URL right now can" >&2
  echo "  set the administrator password and own every connection you add later." >&2
  echo "  Cause: CB_SERVER_NAME, CB_ADMIN_NAME and CB_ADMIN_PASSWORD must ALL three be set." >&2
  fail=1
elif ! grep -q '"configurationMode":false' "$TMP/cfg"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: no configurationMode field in the response. It moved; do not assume it is" >&2
  echo "  closed on the strength of an absent field." >&2
  exit 2
else
  echo "OK: configuration is finished, so the wizard cannot be used to claim this instance."
fi

if grep -q '"anonymousAccessEnabled":true' "$TMP/cfg"; then
  echo "FAIL: anonymous access is ENABLED. Set CLOUDBEAVER_APP_ANONYMOUS_ACCESS_ENABLED=false" >&2
  echo "  and redeploy before you add any connection to this instance." >&2
  fail=1
elif ! grep -q '"anonymousAccessEnabled":false' "$TMP/cfg"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: no anonymousAccessEnabled field in the response." >&2
  exit 2
else
  echo "OK: anonymous access is disabled."
fi

if grep -q '"supportsCustomConnections":true' "$TMP/cfg"; then
  echo "NOTE: non-admin users can create their own connections. That is a deliberate setting;" >&2
  echo "  it also lets any account open TCP connections from this VM into your private network." >&2
fi

[ "$fail" -eq 0 ] || exit 1
echo
echo "Last step, and HTTP cannot do it for you: sign in at https://$HOST with the admin account"
echo "you were given. A server can be out of configuration mode and still have credentials you"
echo "do not hold, so the only proof the instance is YOURS is logging into it."

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove this CloudBeaver is configured, owned by you, and not open to anonymous visitors.
#   ./verify-cloudbeaver.sh cloudbeaver-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
# Exit 0 = good, 1 = FAIL (fix it now), 2 = inconclusive (it may still be starting).
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-cloudbeaver.sh <host>}"
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# 1. GATE. /status is CloudBeaver's own unauthenticated status servlet. Without this gate every
#    assertion below is vacuous, because redu's proxy answers 502 while the container starts and an
#    error page fails every "did it NOT do X" check. A JVM this size takes a while, so be patient.
code=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/status" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/status")
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /status answered HTTP $code, not 200." >&2
  if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
    echo "  502 is redu's proxy while the container starts. Wait and re-run. This is NOT a pass." >&2
  fi
  exit 2
fi
if ! grep -q '"health"' "$TMP/status" || ! grep -q '"product.name"' "$TMP/status"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 200 from /status but the body is not CloudBeaver's status payload." >&2
  exit 2
fi
echo "OK: CloudBeaver is serving."

# 2. POSITIVE CONTROL. Ask its GraphQL API for the server config. If this does not come back with a
#    version and a name, nothing below means anything. Body on stdin, never in argv.
printf '%s' '{"query":"{serverConfig{name version configurationMode anonymousAccessEnabled supportsCustomConnections}}"}' > "$TMP/q"
code=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/cfg" -w '%{http_code}' -X POST \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @"$TMP/q" "https://$HOST/api/")
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: POST /api/ answered HTTP $code." >&2
  exit 2
fi
if ! grep -q '"version"' "$TMP/cfg" || ! grep -q '"name"' "$TMP/cfg"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /api/ returned 200 without a serverConfig payload. Do not read the flags" >&2
  echo "  below out of a body this script could not identify." >&2
  exit 2
fi

# 3. THE ASSERTIONS. Each one requires the field to be PRESENT with the right value. A missing
#    field is inconclusive, never a pass, because a renamed field would otherwise read as success.
fail=0
if grep -q '"configurationMode":true' "$TMP/cfg"; then
  echo "FAIL: this server is STILL IN CONFIGURATION MODE. Anyone who loads the URL right now can" >&2
  echo "  set the administrator password and own every connection you add later." >&2
  echo "  Cause: CB_SERVER_NAME, CB_ADMIN_NAME and CB_ADMIN_PASSWORD must ALL three be set." >&2
  fail=1
elif ! grep -q '"configurationMode":false' "$TMP/cfg"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: no configurationMode field in the response. It moved; do not assume it is" >&2
  echo "  closed on the strength of an absent field." >&2
  exit 2
else
  echo "OK: configuration is finished, so the wizard cannot be used to claim this instance."
fi

if grep -q '"anonymousAccessEnabled":true' "$TMP/cfg"; then
  echo "FAIL: anonymous access is ENABLED. Set CLOUDBEAVER_APP_ANONYMOUS_ACCESS_ENABLED=false" >&2
  echo "  and redeploy before you add any connection to this instance." >&2
  fail=1
elif ! grep -q '"anonymousAccessEnabled":false' "$TMP/cfg"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: no anonymousAccessEnabled field in the response." >&2
  exit 2
else
  echo "OK: anonymous access is disabled."

content.text:
**CloudBeaver is live and verified.**

## https://cloudbeaver-exhrqhde.redu.cloud

| | |
|---|---|
| **Username** | `cbadmin` |
| **Password** | `«REDACTED:entropy:6f102849»` |

Save that password now — it's only in this session, deliberately not in any file. It's already in CloudBeaver's internal database, so changing `CB_ADMIN_PASSWORD` on a later redeploy does nothing; change it from the UI.

**Verification passed (exit 0).** `serverConfig` reports `configurationMode: false`, `anonymousAccessEnabled: false`, `supportsCustomConnections: false`, and `name: "CloudBeaver on redu"` — the server name I set, which is your proof the auto-configuration ran rather than a stranger finishing the wizard. The setup wizard was never open on the public hostname.

**Your managed Postgres** — enter these under Administration → Connections (PostgreSQL driver, already bundled in the image):

| | |
|---|---|
| Host | `[ip]` (private network only) |
| Port | `5432` |
| Database | `app` |
| User | `appuser` |

The password isn't exposed through the API, and my SSH attempt to read it was blocked by the permission classifier. Run this yourself:

```
! ssh -i ~/.ssh/redu-deploy-test -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -p 22021 ubuntu@cloudbeaver-exhrqhde.redu.cloud 'sudo grep ^PGPASSWORD= «REDACTED:assigned:d152c210»'
```

**Cost:** £0.0452/hr, ~£33/mo — app VM £0.0278 + Postgres £0.0174. `plan_deploy` wanted m1.large at £48/mo; `flavor_id: "3"` held m1.medium, confirmed on the real VM. Boot took ~300s.

**Two things to know.** The managed Postgres is the database CloudBeaver *manages*, not where it stores itself — its admin account, users, and every saved connection with its credentials live in the H2 database inside the `cloudbeaver-workspace` volume. Lose that volume and the instance comes back unconfigured and unclaimed. And `delete_deployment` destroys the app VM *and* that volume while deliberately leaving the Postgres behind, still billing at £0.0174/hr; tearing down all of it needs `delete_database` too.

**One correction to the recipe.** `redu.md`'s own verification script was broken in two independent ways, and I fixed both: the GraphQL endpoint is `/api/gql`, not `/api/` (which is the servlet root and 405s on POST), and CloudBeaver pretty-prints its JSON, so the `"field":false` greps could never match. Either bug alone made the script exit `2 INCONCLUSIVE` against a completely healthy server. Both failed closed rather than into a false pass, which is the design working as intended.

Files written: `docker-compose.yml`, `verify-cloudbeaver.sh` (fixed, executable), `redu-deploy-plan.md` (real deployed values), and `redu.md` updated with `last_deploy`, the deploy log, and five new quirks — including the measured boot time and both script bugs, so the next run doesn't rediscover them.
